questions.q: What does a testing environment need that a development environment deliberately doesn't, per this lesson?
options: Faster CPU allocation than any other environment
Direct write access for every user in the company
Data realistic enough to surface real bugs, and a place for checks beyond just the original developer's own testing
A permanent connection to the live production database
questions.explain: Development optimizes for speed and isolation with no real data required; testing needs data realistic enough to catch bugs that only appear at real scale, plus independent checks beyond the builder's own testing.

questions.q: Which kind of testing specifically checks that pieces which depend on each other -- like a Flow calling an Apex action -- still work correctly once combined?
options: Unit testing
Load testing
Regression-only testing
Integration testing
questions.explain: Integration testing checks interdependent pieces working together once combined, which this lesson identifies as the core work of the testing tier.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Partial Copy sandboxes are the usual fit for integration testing and UAT?
options: Because they offer a realistic sample of actual production data via a sandbox template, without the full cost and refresh time of a Full sandbox
Because Partial Copy sandboxes are the only sandbox type that supports Flows
Because Partial Copy sandboxes automatically fix any bugs they find
Because Partial Copy sandboxes are free in every Salesforce edition
questions.explain: A Partial Copy sandbox gives testers real data shapes and realistic edge cases that hand-built test data in a Developer sandbox typically misses, without the cost of a complete Full-sandbox replica.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that the person who built a change shouldn't be the only person testing it?
options: Because developers are legally barred from testing their own code
Because a builder's own test only confirms the change does what they intended, which says nothing about whether they intended the right thing or missed an effect elsewhere in the org
Because independent testers always find more bugs due to having more experience
Because Salesforce requires a minimum of three testers per change by policy
questions.explain: Independent testing catches the gap between 'works as the builder expected' and 'works as the business actually needs' -- a gap the builder's own testing is structurally unable to reveal.

questions.q: What should happen when a change fails testing at this tier, per this lesson's framing of the promotion path?
options: It should be promoted to Staging anyway, so Staging can double-check whether it's really a problem
It should be deployed directly to production with a note to monitor it closely
It goes back to Development for a fix, and the fixed version re-enters testing from scratch
The testing environment should be deleted and recreated to clear the error
questions.explain: The promotion path's entire point is that nothing advances past a stage it hasn't actually passed -- a failed test sends the change back to Development, not forward.
